premises.text: Companies are flying blind on supplier environmental sustainability while scandals keep appearing
premises.evidence_span: companies have very little information and are flying blind

premises.text: Sustainability reporting norms have shifted fast, with Fortune 500 reporting jumping from 20% to 57% in one year
premises.evidence_span: Fortune 500 companies' sustainability reporting has gone from 20% to 57% just between 2010 and 2011

premises.text: One integrated platform handles scorecards, on-the-fly risk analysis, and supplier management for buyers
premises.evidence_span: the first truly integrated platform that helps companies understand and manage their supply chain sustainability

premises.text: Supplier-facing dashboards showing industry-peer standing turn questionnaire burden into improvement incentives
premises.evidence_span: Right now, suppliers are inundated with questionnaires that they fill out and send back, and they have no idea where they stand. This helps them.

premises.text: Cross-network visibility of anonymous supplier scores routes business toward more sustainable suppliers
premises.evidence_span: buyers have access to more sustainable suppliers, and more sustainable suppliers get more business

premises.text: Enrolled suppliers pay an annual fee plus a small per-supplier fee
premises.evidence_span: once suppliers enroll, they pay a annual fee plus a small fee per supplier

value.text: Buyers know exactly which suppliers to use and avoid environmental-disaster headlines
value.evidence_span: they will know exactly which suppliers to use. And they'll know that they won't have to deal with environmental disaster headlines.

causal_links.evidence_span: consumers, shareholders, and the media are increasingly paying attention
understand and manage their supply chain sustainability
more sustainable suppliers get more business

notes: Folded reading: drill-down analysis, questionnaire scorecards, the unified library, and the remaining feature list are parts of one buyer-platform offering (v1.3.2 clarification 5), giving singleton D2 — retained because the buyer-side product is learned and sold as a unit apart from the supplier-side network dynamics. Fee premise grouped with the supplier network because enrollment and payment are one supplier-side motion. No dependency coded this run: the incentive story is asserted but its warrant overlaps domain membership, and 4.4 says omit when in doubt.
